record.original_question: Let T_b(A) denote a paracommutator determined by a Fourier kernel A and symbol b. Develop a general theory for vector-valued or operator-valued paracommutators analogous to the scalar theory, including criteria that characterize boundedness, compactness, and membership in Schatten-von Neumann classes for these vector or operator versions.

evidence.quote: Remark. It is also of interest to consider vector or operator versions of paracommutators. For instance, “big” Hankel operators in the sense of Axler [A] can in principle at least be reduced to suitable vectorial paracommutators. But, as far as we know, no general theory has yet been worked out in this case.

artifact.status_search_result: A complete general theory of vector- or operator-valued paracommutators characterizing boundedness, compactness, and Schatten-class membership analogous to the scalar Janson–Peetre theory does not appear to have been worked out in full generality. Subsequent work extended the scalar theory (e.g. to product spaces and to paraproducts via p-John–Nirenberg theorems), and partial results exist for operator-valued Hankel/Toeplitz analogues, but a unified treatment for vector/operator paracommutators seems not to have been established.

status_evidence.title: Paracommutators on Product Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Boundedness and Schatten-von Neumann properties of paracommutators on product spaces are characterized by membership of their symbols in BMO and Besov spaces on product spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Extensions of the scalar paracommutator theory continue in special settings, but vector/operator versions are not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Paraproducts and Hankel operators of Schatten class via p-John–Nirenberg Theorem
status_evidence.snippet: Schatten-class characterizations for paraproducts and Hankel operators.
status_evidence.claim: Related scalar developments exist; no unified operator-valued paracommutator theory is identified.
